mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Company Extract (Companies Register search result evidencing name clearance, reservation and non-identical availability)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies — New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a New Zealand notary public, followed by Hague Apostille issued by the Department of Internal Affairs (Authentications Unit); for non-Hague destination jurisdictions requiring full chain-authentication, consular legalization at the destination country's consulate in Wellington is added after the apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and extract of registered office, directors, and issued capital of the International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies — New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit); where the receiving bank, payment processor, or overseas regulator does not accept apostille, a New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade legalization certificate plus destination-consulate consular legalization is obtained

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Significant Controllers Register (statutory declaration of ultimate beneficial owners prepared at incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Director(s) of the International Company and the licensed corporate services provider (reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Statutory declaration made before a New Zealand notary public, then Hague Apostille; the bundle is additionally submitted to consular legalization by the destination country's embassy in New Zealand wherever the counterparty jurisdiction is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Office Agent Consent and Appointment Letter (physical New Zealand address and service-of-process acceptance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand licensed corporate services provider / registered office agent (AML/CFT reporting entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille; supplementary consular legalization for bank/KYC panels in jurisdictions that insist on embassy certification of corporate agent documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, shareholder, significant controller, and ultimate beneficial owner against the New Zealand Consolidated Sanctions List administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, and the New Zealand Police Proceeds of Crime/Financial Intelligence financial information; prudent-practice screening additionally applies the OFAC SDN List and FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists given the cross-border payment rails; foreign PEPs and their close family/associates trigger enhanced due diligence and senior-manager approval under section 23 and Part 2 of the AML/CFT Act 2009; standard risk-tiering for a low-risk TikTok Shop retail entity applies but does not waive identity verification and beneficial ownership statement requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register — Companies Office (MBIE) portal: https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in English, te reo Māori, or other languages, but the Registrar may require an accurate English transliteration to be entered in the register; the name must be expressed in ordinary script and may not consist solely of punctuation, graphical symbols, or characters incapable of being reproduced in the register's record; every limited liability company name must terminate with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Tapui', or such variant approved under section 21(2) of the Companies Act 1993; a name will be refused if it is identical or nearly identical to an existing reserved or registered name, or if its use would likely mislead the public or breach intellectual-property rights.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is rejected, the applicant receives a written Registrar's decision stating the statutory ground under section 20 or section 21 of the Companies Act 1993. An administrative reconsideration may be submitted within 20 working days of the decision, attaching evidence of distinctiveness, prior use, or governmental/ministerial consent where the objection concerns a restricted token. The Registrar must reconsider under sections 20–21 and may issue a revised decision. If the refusal stands, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016, naming the Registrar as respondent, within the ordinary limitation period; alternatively, a fresh, materially distinct name may be reserved immediately without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A New Zealand registered office must be a real, physical street address within New Zealand where legal documents can be served; a Post Office Box is strictly prohibited. Virtual-office products are accepted only when anchored to a licensed corporate services provider that maintains a physical registered-office address in New Zealand, consents to act as agent for service, and maintains the significant controllers register at that address. For a non-resident-owned International Company relying on the Income Tax Act 2007 s HR 8 exemption, the Inland Revenue will examine whether the central management and control or any New Zealand-source activity creates taxable substance; therefore a bare non-substantive virtual mailbox without a locally engaged agent, books, and officer support materially elevates compliance and tax re-characterisation risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for a compliant, low-risk retail social-commerce entity: approximately 15% per annum probability of an unannounced physical visit by the Companies Office or an FMA/sector supervisor where the IC uses a licensed agent with a true physical registered office; the probability increases to approximately 35% per annum if the registered office is an unanchored virtual mailbox, if beneficial ownership documentation is incomplete, or if the entity triggers AML/CFT disclosure events.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1981–82 (Cook Islands) (as amended), ss. 3, 6–9, 11, 12, 20, 21, 30, 47; Financial Services Development Authority Act 2016 (CK), ss. 10–15; supplemental application of the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss. 16–20 and Part 18 (overseas company registration), all administered within the unified sovereign framework of the Realm of New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Financial Services Development Authority (FSDA), Rarotonga, Cook Islands; New Zealand liaison registry: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company, together with the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association, the consent of the licensed registered agent, and the tax-exempt status election under s. 30 of the International Companies Act 1981–82 (filed through the FSDA eRegistry portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under s. 8 of the International Companies Act 1981–82. Share capital may be denominated in any currency and may be of no par value; the initial subscriber typically subscribes for one or more ordinary shares at par. No escrow account, capital deposit, bank reference, or paid-up capital certification is required at incorporation or at any time thereafter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] (incorporated under the International Companies Act 1981–82 (Cook Islands)). RESOLVED THAT: (1) The Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Registrar of International Companies be and hereby are adopted, and the incorporation of the Company as an International Company is acknowledged. (2) The initial subscriber be and is hereby allotted [e.g. 100] ordinary shares of no par value, fully subscribed at par, and the allotment be recorded in the Register of Members without any call, escrow, or paid-up capital deposit. (3) The registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [address of licensed registered agent], Rarotonga, Cook Islands, and the licensed registered agent is authorized to receive statutory notices and process service on the Company's behalf. (4) [Name of appointee] be and is hereby appointed as the first director and [Name of appointee] be and is hereby appointed as company secretary, each to hold office until the first annual general meeting or until earlier removal by ordinary resolution. (5) The director is authorized to open banking and payment-account relationships, to appoint the resident agent, and to execute all instruments necessary to give effect to this resolution. Dated: [date]. Certified by: [company secretary].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FSDA Name Registry, Financial Services Development Authority (Cook Islands), acting through an FSDA-licensed International Company Service Provider; name availability cross-check with the New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name reservation request (Form NC-1) through an FSDA-licensed service provider on the FSDA eRegistry portal. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name already on the Companies Register and must not include a restricted word (e.g., Bank, Trust, Insurance) absent a specific statutory licence. Where the International Company will later carry on business in New Zealand, verify that the same name is also available on the New Zealand Companies Register. Provide a declaration confirming the name's distinctiveness and absence of any connection with a prohibited or sanctioned entity.
required_dossiers: Completed Form NC-1 (name reservation)
Proposed company name and statement of business purpose
Declaration of name distinctiveness
Ultimate beneficial owner KYC/identification documents
Letter of engagement from the FSDA-licensed service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses or queries the name under ss. 14–16 of the International Companies Act 1981–82, the applicant may submit a revised name application without loss of priority or file written submissions in support of the original name; the Registrar must issue a final determination within 10 business days of receiving the submissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Licensed Registered Agent and Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Development Authority (FSDA) Licensing Department, Cook Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Registered Agency Agreement (Form RA-1) with an FSDA-licensed International Company Service Provider. The agreement appoints the agent to maintain the statutory registered office at its approved Rarotonga address and to act as resident agent under s. 12 of the International Companies Act 1981–82. The agent will collect the corporate KYC pack, verify the subscriber and any beneficial owners, and issue its certificate of consent to act as registered agent.
required_dossiers: Signed Registered Agency Agreement (Form RA-1)
Valid FSDA licence of the appointed service provider
Passport and proof of address of each director and subscriber
Beneficial ownership declaration and corporate chart (if applicable)
Client due diligence questionnaire completed by the ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensed agent declines to act or the FSDA objects to the appointment, the applicant shall engage an alternate FSDA-licensed provider; the consent certificate is re-issued and forwarded to the Registrar without any additional government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FSDA Registration Department (scrutiny); documents prepared by the licensed agent or corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with ss. 8 and 9 of the International Companies Act 1981–82. The Memorandum must state the company name, registered office, objectives, and share capital structure; the Articles must address director powers, board meeting procedure, share transfer, indemnity, and the tax-exempt status election under s. 30. Execute the documents in the presence of a witness; for foreign subscribers, notarization or apostille is recommended to facilitate the FSDA's acceptance and subsequent bank due diligence by payment partners.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association
Draft Articles of Association
Subscriber signature page with witness details
Notarized identity documents for each foreign subscriber
Name reservation confirmation from the FSDA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSDA returns the constitutional documents for correction (e.g., a prohibited objective, defective share clause, or non-compliant indemnity provision), the licensed agent will amend and re-submit through the portal; corrected filings are processed within 3 business days of re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Government Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Financial Services Development Authority (FSDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically file Form 1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company) on the FSDA eRegistry portal, attaching the executed Memorandum and Articles, the registered agent's consent, the declaration of tax-exempt status under s. 30 of the Act, and payment of the US$500 government incorporation fee plus the licensed agent's statutory facilitation fee. The application receives an automatic acknowledgement and then proceeds to substantive statutory scrutiny by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Form 1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent of the licensed registered agent
Notice of tax-exempt status election under s. 30
Government fee receipt (US$500)
Declaration of non-resident ownership, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition, the applicant has 14 days to file a supplementary reply; non-compliance deems the application withdrawn, with the right to re-file. The applicant may seek reconsideration by written request to the FSDA Registrar within 10 days of the refusal; any misunderstanding of the documentation is cured without additional state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Financial Services Development Authority (FSDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar signs and seals the Certificate of Incorporation and registers the constitutional documents. The licensed agent shall collect the original Certificate and prepare the corporate kit, including printed share certificates, a company seal, the registers of members, directors, charges, and the statutory minute book.
required_dossiers: Approved FSDA incorporation file
Original Certificate of Incorporation
Company seal and pre-printed share certificates
Statutory registers (register of members, directors, and charges)
Memorandum and Articles as registered by the FSDA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a typographical or legal error, the company may apply under s. 20 of the International Companies Act 1981–82 for rectification; the Registrar must correct the register within 5 business days of receiving the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of First Director and Secretary; Bank and Payment-Rails Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The board acting under the International Companies Act 1981–82; AML/CFT compliance units of banking and payment partners, including Wise B2B and TikTok Shop Payout
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution to appoint the first director and company secretary and to ratify the registered office. Issue certified extracts of the First Board Resolution for use by counterparties. Open the Wise B2B account and register the TikTok Shop seller account, submitting the corporate due diligence pack to satisfy each provider's AML/CFT customer identification and beneficial ownership requirements.
required_dossiers: Certified extract of the First Board Resolution
Certificate of Incorporation
Register of directors and members
Beneficial ownership declaration
AML/KYC forms of the payment provider (Wise and TikTok Shop)
Source-of-funds statement or bank reference, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a payment partner raises enhanced due diligence queries, provide notarized statements of source of wealth and expected sales volumes; adverse determinations may be appealed through the partner's internal review process within 14 days or remediated by selecting an alternate licensed payment rail.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: New Zealand Overseas-Company Registration and IRD Tax-Registration (where trading into or from New Zealand)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE); Inland Revenue Department (New Zealand)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the International Company acquires any physical presence, marketplace nexus, or trading activity in New Zealand, file Form CK with the New Zealand Companies Office, appoint a New Zealand agent for service of process (Form NZA), and record the certified constitutional documents. Simultaneously apply to Inland Revenue for a New Zealand IRD number; register for New Zealand GST only if taxable supplies exceed the NZ$60,000 registration threshold; confirm that no New Zealand source income is derived that would create a fixed establishment or permanent establishment under New Zealand tax law.
required_dossiers: Form CK (overseas company registration)
Form NZA (appointment of agent for service of process)
Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
Certified Memorandum and Articles of Association (with English translation, if necessary)
IRD registration application for a non-resident company IRD number
Declaration of non-resident status and tax-exempt character under the International Companies Act 1981–82
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the New Zealand Companies Office requires corrections, refile amended particulars within 20 business days; a refusal to register may be appealed to the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993, and any IRD assessment or registration decision may be objected to under Part 8A of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to a purely digital social-commerce operation. Online marketplace conduct is supervised by the Commerce Commission New Zealand under the Fair Trading Act 1986 and by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) for business registration and consumer policy; no industrial or manufacturing licensing board is engaged because the entity has no physical production or retail premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial, retail-trade, or operating licence is mandated for the TikTok Shop social-commerce model. The operator must complete (i) TikTok Shop Seller Registration under the platform's merchant terms, (ii) New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registration if a New Zealand nexus arises, and (iii) any trade-specific registration under the Fair Trading Act 1986 governing direct-to-consumer representations and online advertising.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no Environmental Impact Assessment or resource consent is required under the Resource Management Act 1991 for a non-transactional digital service with no physical discharges; the activity constitutes a Permitted Activity in the absence of any land-use, discharge, or emissions trigger.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-waste discharge is generated by the digital commerce operation. If the operator later introduces third-party warehousing, storage, or fulfilment, the applicable compliance thresholds are the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ) for VOC and particulate emissions, the Resource Management Act 1991 discharge consent regime for any trade wastewater, and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 for due-diligence on waste handlers and the hazardous substances controls under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for the non-physical digital operation. Should a physical office or warehouse be established in New Zealand, clearance must be obtained from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) for fire-safety certification, from the relevant territorial authority for Building Act 2004 code compliance and structural-load approval, and from WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for workplace registration and worker-engagement obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; primary digital portal is myIR (secure online services at www.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident offshore entity (such as an International Company) must first determine whether it is tax resident in New Zealand. Under New Zealand domestic law, a company is tax resident if it is incorporated in New Zealand, has its head office in New Zealand, or its centre of management is in New Zealand. A foreign-incorporated International Company that does not meet these tests is non-resident. To obtain a statutory New Zealand TIN (IRD number) and, where required, a GST/VAT registration number, the foreign entity must submit Form IR596 ('Non-resident company IRD number application') to Inland Revenue, either online through the myIR portal or by paper submission, accompanied by authenticated copies of the certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, constitutional documents, directors' and shareholders' identification, and a certified statement confirming no New Zealand fixed establishment or residential management nexus. Upon issuance of the IRD number, if the entity intends to make taxable supplies in New Zealand or is required under the remote services rules to collect GST, it must file Form GST1A (or register online via myIR) selecting the 'non-resident supplier of remote services' category. The entity must also designate a New Zealand agent for service of notices if it has no physical presence. Registration is subject to Inland Revenue's anti-fraud verification and may take 5–15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box election akin to the U.S. Treasury regulations. Instead, entity classification follows statutory residency tests and the Uniform Company Tax Code. For a non-resident International Company that is centrally managed and controlled outside New Zealand and has no New Zealand permanent establishment, no entity-level or flow-through election is required or available; the entity remains outside the New Zealand income tax net. However, New Zealand has targeted hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act 2007 (subpart FH) that deny deductions for certain hybrid financial instrument payments, imports of hybrid mismatch tax benefits, and reverse hybrid structures. Domestic close-held companies may elect to be taxable as Look-Through Companies (LTC) under sections HB 1–HB 7 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and, for limited partnerships, flow-through treatment applies by default. These domestic elections are not available to non-resident International Companies, which instead rely on application of the offshore entity exemption and applicable double tax agreements to remain tax-transparent or tax-neutral in New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 per 12-month period for taxable supplies supplied in New Zealand, including supplies of remote services by non-resident suppliers to New Zealand resident consumers; lower threshold of NZD 0 applies where the non-resident supplier uses a New Zealand marketplace facility to supply imported goods and has no physical presence
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls. There is no government-operated mandatory e-invoicing or clearance API for GST. Tax invoices and credit notes must be issued in a paper or electronic format containing statutory content under section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Since 2021, Inland Revenue has supported voluntary PEPPOL BIS 3.0 e-invoicing through the PEPPOL network, but no real-time transmission to Inland Revenue is required. Under the TikTok Shop retail model, the platform retailer must issue an electronic invoice or tax receipt to each New Zealand consumer; where the supply is zero-rated for export, the outward evidence must be retained. Online marketplaces are required to file an electronic marketplace GST return using myIR and may be liable as deemed supplier under section 60(1C) for imported goods and remote services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of export supplies is allowed under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Goods are zero-rated if the supplier exports them within 28 days of the time of supply, and the supplier retains sufficient evidence that the goods have left New Zealand. Services are zero-rated if the supply is made to a non-resident recipient and the benefit of the services is received entirely outside New Zealand, or the services relate to land or moveable goods located outside New Zealand, subject to the recipient being outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed. For goods supplied to a TikTok Shop customer in an offshore jurisdiction, the goods must be physically exported from New Zealand (or, if supplied by a non-resident seller from a third country, no New Zealand GST arises). A non-resident International Company selling into New Zealand from offshore is not required to charge New Zealand GST on B2C remote services if its global turnover is below the NZD 60,000 threshold; above that, the non-resident supplier is liable to register and charge NZ GST. Exported goods zero-rating requires that the supplier retain proof of export contemporaneously with the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NZCS Electronic Export Declaration (Cargo Entry) lodged via the New Zealand Customs Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or courier waybill evidencing dispatch from New Zealand to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice or tax invoice referencing the zero-rated export supply and the overseas consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/FX payment confirmation from the offshore buyer proving payment in foreign currency
Export evidence log (purchase order, packing list, and proof of departure from New Zealand port or airport)
Third-party logistics or freight forwarder certificate of export where the transaction is intermediated by TikTok Shop fulfilment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand Inland Revenue has a robust export zero-rating enforcement regime. If an exporter fails to provide satisfactory evidence of export within the statutory timeline, the supply is recharacterized as standard-rated and GST becomes payable at 15%, with use-of-money interest running from the original due date. Additionally, under the Tax Administration Act 1994, a false GST return or deliberate attempt to zero-rate an ineligible domestic supply attracts severe penalties: a shortfall penalty of 20% for unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or similar offence. Individuals involved in fraudulent export-rebate schemes may be prosecuted and subject to imprisonment. GST refunds arising from zero-rated exports are subject to Inland Revenue integrity checks, including pre-refund audits and regional risk profiling; refund claims may be held pending verification of the entire export transaction chain. There is no statutory repatriation requirement of export proceeds, but for GST zero-rating, documentary proof of payment must be available; where proceeds are not repatriated to a New Zealand bank account within 180 days, Inland Revenue will scrutinize whether the supply actually occurred and whether a sham arrangement exists.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ / Te Pūtea Matua) is the central bank and banking regulator; foreign-exchange administration is decentralised across RBNZ for banking and settlement system oversight, the Financial Markets Authority for financial market conduct and derivatives, and the Department of Internal Affairs for AML/CFT supervision. New Zealand maintains no centralised exchange-control office and imposes no general foreign-exchange licensing on ordinary corporate treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand is a full-currency-convertibility jurisdiction which accepts IMF Article VIII obligations. The New Zealand dollar is freely convertible for both current account and capital account transactions, including sales proceeds, dividends, interest, royalties, intercompany loan repayments and equity repatriation. There are no queues, quotas, conversion tiers or prior central-bank approvals for routine treasury movements. The only material constraints are: (i) anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism verification by banks; (ii) tax withholding obligations on income sourced in New Zealand; (iii) the Overseas Investment Act 2005 screening for sensitive land and significant business assets; and (iv) the obligation to make accurate Balance of Payments and CRS/FATCA-related declarations. Profit remittance from an eligible International Company is not subject to a remittance licence or export certificate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand abolished foreign-exchange controls in the 1980s and currently imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters and cross-border e-commerce sellers may retain receipts in foreign currency indefinitely, either in onshore foreign-currency bank accounts or in offshore accounts, and conversion to New Zealand dollars is optional. The relevant statutory and regulatory disciplines are evidentiary: export receipts must be traceable to underlying invoices and shipping or platform settlement records, banks must obtain complete originator and beneficiary information under the AML/CFT Act 2009, and tax returns must be prepared using the applicable foreign-exchange translation method.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High, but exclusively as an ancillary payment and FX execution rail, not as the principal custodial bank. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise Business may lawfully provide cross-border payment initiation and foreign-exchange conversion services to a New Zealand-resident account holder, provided they do not carry on deposit-taking business in New Zealand in breach of the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. Actual holding of customer deposits by a non-bank requires a registered bank licence or an exemption. The EMI must also comply with the AML/CFT Act 2009 if it has a New Zealand nexus or contracts with New Zealand customers, and client funds must be segregated and safeguarded. Execution-only FX payments are permissible; any advice or structured derivative issuance triggers the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. Accordingly, Wise B2B is suitable for TikTok Shop payout collection, supplier disbursements, and FX conversion, while the capital escrow account and core treasury custody must remain with a licensed New Zealand commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no absolute statutory requirement that directors appear physically in New Zealand, but in practice almost all major New Zealand banks treat a non-resident International Company with no local economic substance as a face-to-face onboarding case. A natural person director, authorised officer, or a properly constituted local agent holding a power of attorney must attend a physical KYC meeting in Auckland or Wellington. Remote opening can be considered when the beneficial ownership chain is transparent, all corporate documents are apostilled and notarially certified, and an acceptable bank-to-bank reference from a respectable relationship bank is provided. Beneficial owners with no directorship role may remain offshore if the trust and corporate ownership chain is fully evidenced and source-of-wealth documentation is available for each material owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident International Company with tax-exempt status and no identifiable New Zealand economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, certificate of incumbency, register of directors and shareholders, official tax-exemption or non-assessment notice, trust deed and protector consent establishing the beneficial owner chain, board resolutions for the New Zealand bank account, and a written commercial explanation for the TikTok Shop retail and trade payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face account opening with only electronically copied passport and corporate print
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially certified and apostilled passports of all signatories, proof-of-address documents issued within the last three months, recognised digital identity verification and liveness assurance certificate from the bank-approved provider, original bank reference letter from the entity's existing relationship bank, and a statutory declaration from the local natural-person director verifying the identity and authority of every relevant principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border payment volumes forecasted from social commerce and live-streaming retail without a conventional physical export warehouse
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed TikTok Shop store registration or seller agreement, platform settlement and payout statements, commissioned transaction ledger, contractual supplier orders and proforma invoices, customs or freight forwarding discharge records, inventory sourcing contracts, and a monthly cash-flow forecast matching the expected payout frequency and exposure to supply-chain disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee, trust, or layered shareholding structure making the ultimate beneficial ownership appear opaque
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate ownership chart from each intermediate vehicle down to final natural persons, nominee shareholder declaration and indemnity, trust deed with settlor/appointor/protector/beneficiary definitions, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for every natural person, certified copy of the registered agent's AML/CFT compliance policies, and legal opinion confirming that the structure is not used to evade tax, sanctions, or anti-money-laundering obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipts from TikTok Shop and related offshore intercompany payouts creating a perceived commingling or layering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reconciliation report linking TikTok Shop gross sales to the Wise B2B payout rail and onward sweep to the New Zealand operational account, platform payout-ID tracking, intercompany loan or settlement agreements, group financial statements, bank statements with narrative booking, and an internal accounting policy requiring separation of customer fund receipts, treasury balances, and working capital.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection routing for the International Company utilises SWIFT MT103 for high-value wire transfers or ISO 20022 pain.001 instructions when initiated through an EMI or treasury platform. The payment narrative must expressly state 'Shareholder equity injection' or 'Shareholder loan advance' and reference the New Zealand operational account number and authorised beneficiary name. New Zealand has no mandatory domestic purpose-code regime, but the remitting bank may require a foreign-exchange or Balance-of-Payments purpose indicator such as 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' or 'Other Investment - Loans', which must match the underlying board resolution and intercompany agreement. The receiving bank will verify that the beneficiary name corresponds exactly with KYC records, that signatories are authorised under a current board resolution, and that originator information accompanies the wire. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 only has relevance if the funding is used to acquire sensitive New Zealand land or sensitive business assets, which does not arise in the ordinary TikTok Shop retail model. All funds records, board approvals, source-of-funds documentation, and FX contracts must be retained for at least seven years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements will be cleared using SWIFT MT103 for direct bank-to-bank supplier payments in major currencies, and Commercial Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT707 series where suppliers require documentary compliance. For New Zealand-dollar domestic vendors, the bank will settle through the RBNZ Exchange Settlement Account System and NZClear using the bank's bulk payment gateway. TikTok Shop gross payouts are aggregated by the platform and remitted through the platform payout rail, typically via Wise B2B or an analogous licensed payment aggregator, into the International Company's operational account in New Zealand. The treasury function shall execute FX conversions only upon explicit instruction with a matching underlying invoice, payout statement, or intercompany obligation, thereby preventing unbacked speculative FX exposure. All outgoing remittances must be gold-fish tested against sanctions screening, and full originator and beneficiary fields must comply with AML/CFT wire transfer rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward FX contracts booked with a licensed New Zealand commercial bank for the purchase or sale of USD, CNY, EUR, AUD, GBP against NZD
FX forward rollovers and tom-next swaps used to extend or reset existing commercial hedges without creating speculative exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or less liquid currencies such as CNY, INR, and IDR, cash-settled in NZD or USD against observable published reference rates
Cross-currency swaps for matching the notional principal and interest flows on intercompany shareholder loans and long-term supplier liabilities

Vanilla FX options (calls and puts) written by an authorised derivative issuer when used solely to protect firm committed TikTok Shop sales proceeds and trade payables, subject to Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 issuer and investor eligibility requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form 5 - Annual Return of a Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on the company's Annual Return Date, being the anniversary of incorporation. The filing window opens 25 calendar days before the Annual Return Date and closes at the end of the 5th working day after that date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 200 (approximately USD 122) assessed automatically after the due date. Continued non-compliance triggers a Notice of Intention to Remove the Company from the Register under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993, leading to deregistration, dissolution, and loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Director, Shareholder, and Registered Office Change Notifications
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days of any change in directors, registered office, or address for service, or as such changes arise between annual return dates. The Annual Return reconciles all current details on the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-notification is an offence under the Companies Act 1993; penalties of up to NZD 10,000 per officer may be imposed, and the Registrar may initiate deregistration proceedings for persistent failure to maintain accurate statutory records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Financial Statements and Audit Determination
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office if the entity qualifies as 'large' or is otherwise required to file; otherwise retained at the registered office for inspection by members and the Registrar upon demand.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, financial statements must be completed and tabled within 9 months (by 31 December) and, where a public filing is required, filed with the Registrar within 5 months of balance date (by 31 August).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or file required financial statements is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, with fines up to NZD 50,000 for the company and NZD 10,000 per director; repeated default supports strike-off action by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies where the company is 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (group total assets exceeding NZD 60 million or total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million); where shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights serve a written audit election; where the company's constitution or shareholders' agreement requires audit; or where the Registrar of Companies directs an audit. A private International Company conducting TikTok Shop retail that does not meet these thresholds is exempt from statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (NZ IFRS, equivalent to IFRS as issued by the IASB) for large and publicly accountable entities; Tier 2 NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime for non-publicly accountable entities preparing general purpose financial reports; Tier 3 or Tier 4 simplified cash-based frameworks for small entities. Foreign parent companies may apply an approved foreign GAAP only where the entity qualifies for an exemption under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand maintains no public beneficial ownership register. The company must keep an accurate internal Register of Members reflecting all share transfers. Prior to each Annual Return, the registered agent must confirm that the listed shareholders are the true legal holders and that any UBO changes (including transfers of substantive control) have been verified under the AML/CFT Act 2009 customer due diligence obligations and recorded in the entity's share transfer records. Every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members upon presentation of the instrument of transfer, with an internal UBO attestation completed within 30 days of the transfer and no later than the next Annual Return filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board and Shareholder Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500-1,500 per annum for registered office, company secretary, and resident compliance agent services for a New Zealand International Company
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-8,000 per annum for a certified independent audit of a small to mid-sized e-commerce retail entity, where an audit is elected or triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not operate territorial tax holidays or free-zone corporate income tax exemptions. The headline 28% rate can produce a 0% effective result only where a qualifying non-resident foreign company, including a CK_IC International Company, has no New Zealand-source income and no permanent establishment in New Zealand. For New Zealand-resident and PE-taxable companies, available incentives include the 15% refundable R&D tax incentive, depreciation benefits, and the loss offset regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 — Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through Inland Revenue (IRD) myIR online portal or IRD-approved tax agent software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July following the income year. A non-standard balance date requires filing by the 7th day of the 7th month after balance date. Tax agents may obtain an extension to 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity residency status: resident company, non-resident foreign company, or registered foreign company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select non-resident foreign company status; disclose whether the company is centrally managed and controlled in New Zealand to avoid inadvertent tax residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IRD number and registered name exactly matching the certificate of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the New Zealand IRD number issued to the foreign company; do not use an individual tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income derived during the income year from all New Zealand sources
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only New Zealand-source income, including TikTok Shop sales attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment; foreign-source income of a non-resident is not taxable in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenditure and allowable expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses incurred in deriving New Zealand-source income; head-office charges must be arm's length and supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile to management accounts prepared from TikTok Shop payout data and Wise B2B settlement records.
Include penalties, entertainment disallowances, and non-arm's-length payments to related foreign entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses and loss offsets utilised in the current year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company may offset losses only against the same New Zealand-source taxable business activity; foreign losses are not available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss offset and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company has no New Zealand permanent establishment and no New Zealand-source income, enter nil and attach the non-resident status schedule if requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax assessed at 28% on taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the tax at 28%; no preferential company rate applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: resident withholding tax, imputation credits, foreign tax credits, and R&D tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only under a Double Tax Agreement; attach supporting foreign tax assessment documents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax payable or refund due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must pay any residual tax by terminal tax date; late payment penalties apply from that date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: fixed per-month late filing penalty, generally capped at NZ$500 for companies. Late payment penalty: 1% immediately on unpaid tax, an additional 4% after 7 days, and 1% per month thereafter. Further civil penalties apply for knowingly providing false or misleading information.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder claiming a reduced DTA rate must provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence and submit an IR290 Certificate of Residence to the New Zealand paying company before payment. The payer then applies the treaty rate, which for most New Zealand DTAs is 15% on portfolio dividends and, under certain treaties, 5% for substantial shareholdings. If documentation is not furnished before settlement, 30% withholding is applied, with the excess refundable through a New Zealand income tax reassessment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT rates: interest 15%, royalties 15%. Under most New Zealand DTAs, interest is reduced to 10% and royalties to 10% or 15%. For debt securities that qualify, a New Zealand borrower may elect to pay the Approved Issuer Levy at 2% on qualifying interest instead of NRWT, available only where the lender is not associated with the borrower.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZ$10 million aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions; above this threshold the IRD expects contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation consistent with OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines. Below the threshold, arm's-length benchmarking records should still be maintained.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime in the form used by offshore financial centres. However, the general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007, the business-continuity test, and the resident-company central management and control rules impose a substantive economic test. A CK_IC International Company with no local offices, employees, or commercial functions attempting to book New Zealand social commerce profits as tax-exempt will be disregarded and the profits recharacterised to the economic substance owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting TikTok Shop gross sales from the IR4, fabricating supplier invoices, using undisclosed offshore payment wallets, or destroying sales records to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under section 141 of the Tax Administration Act 1994; imprisonment up to 5 years; fines up to NZ$50,000; civil shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax shortfall; use-of-money interest from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in or direct the evasion may be prosecuted personally. The corporate veil may be pierced to collect unpaid source deductions and withholding tax under the director liability provisions; asset freezing and court-imposed travel restrictions are possible under asset recovery and bail procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, IP royalties, marketing fees, or TikTok Shop platform service charges to the New Zealand entity in order to shift profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD adjusts taxable income under sections GC 13 to GC 17 of the Income Tax Act 2007; shortfall penalties range up to 100% for abusive tax positions and 150% for evasion; interest accrues on all adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false tax returns or knowingly approve mispriced related-party transactions face personal civil penalties and potential prosecution for aiding tax evasion; disqualification under the Companies Act 1994 may result.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a CK_IC International Company with no substantive activity, no employees, and no real management outside New Zealand to claim tax-exempt non-resident status while actual TikTok Shop retail management, livestream operations, and inventory decisions occur in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner voids the tax benefit under section BG 1; revenue is recharacterised to the controlling New Zealand resident; shortfall penalties of 100% or 150% apply; foreign company registration may be struck off; treaty benefits are denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed personally if the company is a sham or was used as a mere instrument to avoid tax; courts may order restitution, disqualify directors for up to five years, and impose criminal sanctions for deliberate avoidance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating TikTok Shop retail with high-volume instant payouts through TikTok Shop Payout and Wise B2B without an AML/CFT programme, customer due diligence, sanctions screening, or transaction monitoring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 of up to NZ$2 million per contravention for a body corporate; separate criminal liability for money laundering under the Crimes Act 1961.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, senior managers, and compliance officers can be prosecuted for knowingly permitting suspicious transactions; personal fines up to NZ$200,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years may be imposed, with related travel and occupational restrictions.
